02_dashboards/sales/ISZE_AIM_DB_DLR_Deep.title: AIM deep dive - all distributors with sales-to-dealer data
firstLines: AIM DEEP DIVEALL DISTRIBUTORSRSA
What we billed, against what the distributor sold to its dealers

Both sales stages side by side, always, part number by part number, inside the AIM product tree. Billed is what ISZE invoiced to the distributor. Sold to dealer is what the distributor sold on to its dealer network, on its own report. Built 2026-09-24.

How the euros are read. Sales to dealer arrives with no price of its own, so its euro is modelled and the page says so everywhere it appears. The primary comparison figure is units × the ISZE price list of 10 Aug 2026, so the two stages are measured on the same list. Beside it the page also shows a modelled dealer price: the same figure plus 35% gross margin, which is the price-list euro divided by 0.65. Neither one is the distributor's turnover, its revenue, or an actual dealer purchase price. Only the billed side carries a real invoiced price, so the average actual price and the price index are shown on the billed side alone and no margin is added to them.

Scope badge: RSA sells D-Max to its dealers, and only D-Max. Its sales-to-dealer figures cover light commercial vehicles alone, so they are never added into a truck-family total. Billed units in the same months may include other models.

Common window. In the window you picked, 41 of 44 months carry billing and 12 of 44 carry sales to dealer. Everything that compares the two stages - bought ÷ sold, and PMS cover on both sides - is computed on the months that carry both. Nothing is scaled up and no month is filled in.

No comparison is available on this window. The window and its reference together have to hold billing and sales to dealer in every single month before a comparison can be drawn. A comparison is only shown when both stages cover every month of both windows - twice the window length in total. Nothing is scaled up and no month is filled in.

02_dashboards/sales/ISZE_AIM_Comparison_.title: AIM comparison - all distributors with sales-to-dealer data
firstLines: AIM COMPARISONALL DISTRIBUTORSCV / D-MAX / MIXED, READ PER DISTRIBUTOR BELOW
Which service families and which part numbers grew, and which fell?

Sales to dealer, two equal periods side by side, ranked by the euro that moved, from AIM level 1 down to the single part number. Ranked on sales to dealer, valued at the ISZE price list IE40 PR00 of 10 Aug 2026.
Period A: 2025-01 to 2025-06 against Period B: 2025-07 to 2025-12, 6 months against 6 (the default pair).

This pair is carried by 5 distributors between them: RSA, Ireland, ITUK, IUK, Imotors. Sales to dealer is present in every one of these months for each of them. It is not carried by UTI (missing 2025-02, 2025-03, 2025-04, 2025-05, 2025-06, 2025-07), which this view therefore leaves out entirely rather than filling in. The default pair is the longest equal split the sales-to-dealer data can carry for this selection, cut at the latest month it reaches, and it is the basis for every figure on this page. ISZE billing is shown beside the movement as context only, and it never decides which months are comparable: a month with billing but no sales to dealer is not hidden and is not filled in.

Rule: a comparison of two N-month windows requires 2N unbroken months of sales-to-dealer data. Where that run does not exist, no comparison is drawn at all, and no shorter one is offered as a substitute.

How the euros are read. Sales to dealer arrives with no price of its own, so both periods are valued at the ISZE price list IE40 PR00 of 10 Aug 2026, and the page says so wherever a euro appears. A second figure adds 35% gross margin, which is that price-list euro divided by 0.65, because margin is measured on the selling price. That is a modelled dealer price. It is not the distributor's turnover, not its revenue, and not an actual dealer purchase price. The 35% is an assumption supplied by Jerome; if he meant margin on cost, the price-list euro times 1.35, the figure is about 14% lower.

This view adds the distributors named above together. Their scopes differ, so a part number that only one of them reports is not comparable with one they all report. Use the distributor control to read one of them on its own.
Units not classified in AIM: 4.13% in period A and 2.05% in period B. Units with no price on the list: 1.64% and 1.00%. Both are kept in the figures above, not excluded from them.
DISTRIBUTOR
All distributors with sales-to-dealer data — 44 months of sales to dealer
RSA — 12 months of sales to dealer
Ireland — 19 months of sales to dealer
ITUK — 44 months of sales to dealer
